rationale: C20 is a highly plausible direct drafting template. It presents the 1961 emergency feed-grain program, while the child urges its extension for 1962 and a parallel wheat program. Both texts use the same sequence and nearly the same enumerated policy outcomes: increasing farm income, reducing government costs, reducing surplus grain stocks, and protecting consumers. The child explicitly describes the new wheat program as following the pattern of the Emergency Feed Grain Program and repeats C20's urgency argument that legislation must pass promptly for the relevant crop year. C14 shares the broader agricultural-policy framework but not this distinctive grain-program structure; C16 merely mentions farmers accepting feed-grain limitations.

shared_material.child_excerpt: These programs will accomplish the following results: (1) Increase the income of producers ...; (2) Reduce the ultimate costs to the Government ...; (3) Prevent a further build-up and achieve a moderate reduction in the excessive stocks ...; and (4) Assure ... consumers at reasonable and stable prices
shared_material.parent_excerpt: would accomplish the following: (1) a moderate increase in farm income; (2) a saving of several hundred million dollars of Government funds; and (3) a holding down or reduction of surplus stocks to more manageable proportions. This will be done without any material effect upon consumer prices.
shared_material.explanation: The child closely reproduces C20's distinctive enumerated package of four effects, expanding the final consumer-price point into a fourth numbered item.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Early action on the wheat program is especially needed ... following the pattern being set by the Emergency Feed Grain Program this year. Extension of the 1961 Emergency Feed Grain Program is equally important.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am transmitting herewith a bill to provide a special program for feed grains for 1961. I urgently recommend to the Congress the enactment of this emergency program so that it can cover the 1961 crop.
shared_material.explanation: The child expressly builds its 1962 proposals upon the specific emergency program advocated in C20 and carries forward its crop-year urgency.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The feed grain program should be passed now—not postponed until 1962.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Immediate action is required ... In order to be effective with respect to this year's crops, a new program should be authorized by March 1st.
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same administrative timing argument: enactment must occur immediately so the program can govern the upcoming planting and crop cycle.

shared_material.child_excerpt: If the Emergency Feed Grain Program is not extended, acreage and production in 1962 would increase ... Stocks of grain and costs to the Government would increase once more. Farm income would decline
shared_material.parent_excerpt: If this program is allowed to continue in effect for this year's crop, the stocks in Government hands will reach even more alarming proportions ... farm income will continue to suffer, and large amounts of Government funds will be needlessly expended.
shared_material.explanation: The child adapts C20's linked counterfactual harms—excess production and stocks, higher federal costs, and lower farm income—to the consequences of failing to extend the program.
